Application observed directly with scripted Playwright probes because no Playwright MCP browser tools were exposed this session. Organization Login asks for exactly three details: userName, orgName (Organization Name), password; the sign-in kind is a select#loginType with two options. Missing details produce per-field messages in p#validateTips; wrong details produce one generic refusal in .errorMessage. The two responses differ materially, so AC-ETA-351-008 is satisfiable. Only fabricated credentials were submitted; the real account was withheld because the application warns of lockout, so TS-ETA-351-005 remains unproven until EXECUTION. Three discrepancies recorded without altering any approved expectation: EcoreLogin declares an organizationId the page never asks for; two input[type=submit] controls exist so Sign In must be addressed by accessible name; message containers carry no ARIA role so validated string selectors are unavoidable. AMB-001, AMB-002, AMB-003 and AMB-005 resolved by observation; AMB-004 partially; AMB-006 and CLR-TP-ETA-351-001 remain open human questions. Report: reports/validation/ETA-351-playwright-validation.md

Field locators are scoped to form#eo_cc_login because a hidden forgot-password form duplicates the Username, Organization Name and Business Entity identifiers. Healing attempt 1 of a maximum 2, applied inline because runSubagent is disabled. Two fixes in src/pages/ecore-login.page.ts: (1) expectSignInFailureReported used Locator.or() with toBeVisible, which is a strict-mode violation because both failure containers are always present in the DOM and the unused one is merely hidden via eo-hidden; replaced with independent visibility polling. (2) open() used the default 5s assertion timeout, shorter than the login interstitial 8s scripted fallback redirect; given an explicit 30s budget on an observable state, not a fixed sleep. No approved expectation and no assertion semantics were changed, so Gate 3 did not reopen. Healed on attempt 1; BUG_REPORTING was not entered and no defect artifact was created.

Verified rather than assumed: the generated feature file is byte-identical to the approved one, its eight @ts- tags match the eight approved plan scenarios exactly and in order, and a scan for locators, XPath, css, test ids and page-object calls found nothing.
